programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Countryside Killings: Graham Backhouse
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines why Graham Backhouse attempted to kill his wife with a car bomb before murdering his neighbour in 1984.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Far From Home: Kyu Soo Kim
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines the harrowing case of a London landlord who sadistically tortured and murdered two of his tenants.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Saturday Night Strangler: Joe Kappen
programmes.d: In 1973, three young girls were beaten, raped and strangled over a six-week period. The Saturday Night Strangler escaped justice for almost 30 years. But new techniques in DNA technology and a midnight exhumation finally uncovered the killer.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Double Axe Murderer: Dennis Smalley
programmes.d: A double axe murderer and no clues - except tiny flakes of paint discovered deep in the wounds of one of the victims. This is a story of how forensic science - and the determination of one detective - found the killer.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Into Thin Air: David Gilroy
programmes.d: It was a missing person’s case that shook the people of Scotland to their core. Within a week of Suzanne Pilley disappearing from her place of work in Edinburgh, police were convinced they were hunting for a killer - despite not having found a body.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: At the age of 25, Mark Martin murdered three young women in Nottingham city centre in the winter of 2004-2005. Since his teens, Mark Martin had been fixated on serial killers, and had an ambition to become Nottingham’s first serial killer.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Glyn Dix shot dead his landlady in 1979. While serving a life sentence he met and fell in love with a fellow inmate’s mother. They married, but three years after his release he killed his wife.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: James Fairweather was a 15-year-old boy obsessed with serial killers, violent video games and extreme pornography. He stabbed two strangers to death in separate attacks. He was found unanimously guilty by a jury on 22 April 2016.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Sana Muhammad, formerly known as Devi, had left her unhappy arranged marriage to Ramanodge Unmathallegadoo and remarried. She was a pregnant mother of five when he murdered her in her home.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Stephen Port was convicted of the assaults, rapes and murders of Anthony Walgate, Gabriel Kovari, Daniel Whitworth and Jack Taylor. He was sentenced to life imprisonment with a whole life order.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Secret Torment - I Was Abused By My Father
programmes.d: Alissa Moore was subjected to years of horrific sexual abuse at the hands of her father James O’Brien. Former Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny examine the horrific details of the case.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Disabled Daughter Tortured And Murdered By Her Friends - Gemma Hayter
programmes.d: Former Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny examine Gemma Hayter’s child-like trust in people and look at chilling CCTV recordings that show her being led to her death.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: Our Daughter Murdered In Snuff Movie Fantasy - Georgia Williams
programmes.d: Former Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny give us an insight into Jamie Reynolds’ twisted mind and reveal the full extent of his morbid fascination with extreme violence against women.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Daughter Stalked, Then Murdered By Her Ex - Rana Faruqui
programmes.d: Rana Faruqui’s former boyfriend Stephen Griffiths refused to accept that their relationship, which had only lasted a few months, was over and that Rana wanted nothing more to do with him.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Sister And Her Two Year Old Murdered By Her Ex - Christine Chambers
programmes.d: Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny examine the disturbing details of the horrific double murder of Christine Chambers and her daughter.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Pregnant Daughter Was Strangled To Death By Her Boyfriend - Jayden Parkinson
programmes.d: Jayden, young, beautiful and the new girl, becomes hooked on bad boy Ben Blakely. Despite her friends' warnings that he’s no good for her, Jayden doesn’t listen. However, no one dreamed that he was capable of killing her.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Stepdad Abused Us For 12 Years - Louise Turnbull
programmes.d: Albert Maughan subjected Louise and Craig Turnbull to a harrowing regime of abuse starting from when they were only 3 and 4 years old. 24 years later, Louise decides to put this monster behind bars once and for all.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: Ellie Butler
programmes.d: Britain’s Darkest Taboos tells the stories of some of the most shocking and disturbing crimes within families and relationships. Every family’s worst nightmares are relived and re-told in unflinching detail by those left behind.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: Britain's Darkest Taboos Special - What Makes A Murderer?
programmes.d: In this special episode, we look back over five years and 40 episodes of Britain’s Darkest Taboos and examine what we can learn from some of the most disturbing familial crimes in British criminal history.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Peter Sutcliffe
programmes.d: Arguably Britain's most infamous serial killer, Peter Sutcliffe became known as The Yorkshire Ripper when he began murdering women in Yorkshire during the 1970s.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Christopher Foster
programmes.d: Failed businessman Christopher Foster killed his wife and daughter before burning their mansion in Shropshire to the ground in August 2008.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Marchioness Disaster
programmes.d: The story of the Marchioness; a pleasure boat that collided with dredger Bowbelle and sank within minutes resulting in the loss of 51 lives.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Clare Wood
programmes.d: In April 2007, Clare Wood met George Appleton on a dating website and they embarked on a relationship together. Unbeknownst to her, Appleton was a criminal with a severe history of violence against women.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Suzy Lamplugh
programmes.d: A look at the case of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh, who showed a client around a house in Fulham in July 1986 and was never seen again. Dermot Murnaghan hosts.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Dead Man's Hollow: Nishan Bakunts
programmes.d: In 2002, an off-duty fireman discovered a body in a field charred beyond all recognition. All the police knew was that the man had died a brutal death, having been stabbed repeatedly, shot in the head, and drenched in petrol before being set alight.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Time Of Death: Albert Walker
programmes.d: When a Devonshire fisherman hauled in his nets on July 28 1996, he made a gruesome discovery: among that day’s catch was a dead body. There was nothing to identify the man’s body except a Rolex watch and a small maple leaf tattoo on his hand.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Murder By Mail: Keith Cottingham
programmes.d: In 1984 a parcel bomb was sent to a 53-year-old grandmother living in a tranquil English village. She died of horrific injuries. No one understood why it had happened. The only evidence detectives had was the bomb itself.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Hitman And The Hairdresser: Fadi Nasri
programmes.d: A 29-year-old hairdresser was found brutally stabbed on her doorstep in a quiet suburban street of London. A recording of a threatening phone call seemed to suggest the motive, but every lead comes to a dead end.
